title: Electric basses, five-string basses and wanting a full-size bass
summary: Breaux dislikes electric bass, tried a five-string, notes the E string was removed on some basses, and still wants a full-size bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I was going to ask a little bit about your bass again. You used three quarter size you said. We didn't get all that on the tape I don't think. Oh yeah. You say you don't like the electric bass. No I don't like the electric bass. I mean I'll try them but.
You want to get the true tone to my ear. Out of a amplified bass.
Did you ever try a five string bass? There was a K5 string there. You used with an extra high string.

Yeah I tried that. I played on it but I mean I never used it for my personal stuff. A lot of the bells around here was taken off the E string. Because the E string is so deep. And it's not too very effective. Especially with the.

a big band, a loud dixieland band, so they eliminated the E and brought the A back and stepped and put the C where the G was. I didn't care much for that either. I don't guess too many of them doing it. Somewhere I played not too long ago felt like a bass drum like that.
Do you like a pretty big bass then? At least three-quarter size?
Oh yeah, I like a three-quarter. I mean, I like to get my hands on a full-size bass eventually.
